commands.command: evidence-run semantics review: read repopact/schemas/evidence-run.schema.json in full
commands.summary: The schema imposes no cross-field constraint between top-level `result` and any `commands[].exit_code`. `commands[].exit_code` is required to be an integer, nothing more; `result` is a free-standing enum (passed/failed/partial/blocked) with no conditional relationship to the commands array expressed in the schema.

validate_evidence() performs only structural/referential checks (schema validation, id-matches-filename, duplicate-id detection, ISO-8601 timestamp, work_item existence). It never inspects commands[].exit_code or cross-checks it against result. Confirmed directly from the enforcement code, not inferred.

No explicit prose in SPEC.md defines a relationship between `result` and individual command exit codes beyond listing the required fields -- diagnostic grep, no hits, expected as part of the review rather than a defect (this command's own exit_code reflects the diagnostic search finding nothing, not a gating failure of this work item).

Found direct, accepted precedent: result:"passed" with 2 of 15 commands recording exit_code 1 (a fleet-verify diagnostic that intentionally re-opened known fleet drift, and an S5 selftest failure explicitly routed to proposed WI-037 rather than treated as a WI-033 blocker) alongside 13 commands at exit_code 0.

environment.evidence_run_semantics_conclusion: Schema and validator intentionally permit a passed result alongside non-gating diagnostic command failures. Not a defect. No change made to the evidence-run schema, validate_repo.py, or WI039.
